from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The 'Next-Word' Prediction Game", [
            "LLMs are sophisticated statistical engines.",
            "They predict the next token in sequence.",
            "Given context, they calculate probable outputs."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent LLM as a brain/engine graphic
        brain = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=0.5)
        text_brain = Text("LLM Engine", font_size=20).move_to(brain.get_center())
        engine = VGroup(brain, text_brain)
        self.place_at_grid(engine, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(engine))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE_B))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show sequence of tokens
        token_a = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, color=WHITE).next_to(engine, RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        text_a = Text("The", font_size=18).move_to(token_a.get_center())
        token_b = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, color=WHITE).next_to(token_a, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        text_b = Text("cat", font_size=18).move_to(token_b.get_center())
        
        sequence = VGroup(token_a, text_a, token_b, text_b)
        self.play(Create(sequence))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN_B))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Predict next token
        next_token = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=0.5, color=YELLOW).next_to(token_b, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        text_next = Text("???", font_size=18, color=YELLOW).move_to(next_token.get_center())
        
        prediction = VGroup(next_token, text_next)
        self.play(FadeIn(prediction))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Computers only understand numbers, not text.",
            "Words are mapped to high-dimensional coordinates.",
            "Similar concepts are placed close together."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Embeddings", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        dot_dog = Dot(color=BLUE)
        label_dog = Text("Dog", font_size=20)
        dot_puppy = Dot(color=BLUE)
        label_puppy = Text("Puppy", font_size=20)
        dot_spaceship = Dot(color=RED)
        label_spaceship = Text("Spaceship", font_size=20)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        binary_code = Text("01010101", font_size=30, color=GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_code, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_code))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeOut(binary_code))
        
        # Setup grid/axes for vector space
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "C3")
        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Place words near each other
        pos_dog = axes.c2p(-0.5, -0.5)
        pos_puppy = axes.c2p(-0.3, -0.3)
        pos_spaceship = axes.c2p(1.5, 1.5)
        
        dot_dog.move_to(pos_dog)
        dot_puppy.move_to(pos_puppy)
        dot_spaceship.move_to(pos_spaceship)
        
        label_dog.next_to(dot_dog, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_puppy.next_to(dot_puppy, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_spaceship.next_to(dot_spaceship, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_dog, label_dog, dot_puppy, label_puppy, dot_spaceship, label_spaceship))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Transformers process data differently.", 
            "Attention looks at all words simultaneously.", 
            "This mechanism captures complex context.", 
            "It creates connections between relevant terms.", 
            "Models learn deeper semantic relationships."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Transformer Core: The Self-Attention Mechanism", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        words = ["The", "animal", "didn't", "cross", "the", "street", "because", "it", "was", "too", "tired"]
        word_mobs = VGroup(*[Text(w, font_size=24) for w in words]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(word_mobs, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = [BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        self.play(FadeIn(word_mobs))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        # Highlight all words simultaneously
        self.play(word_mobs.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(colors[3]))
        # Draw line between 'it' and 'animal'
        it_mob = word_mobs[7]
        animal_mob = word_mobs[1]
        line = Line(it_mob.get_top(), animal_mob.get_top(), color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        dot1 = Dot(it_mob.get_top(), color=RED)
        dot2 = Dot(animal_mob.get_top(), color=RED)
        self.play(Create(line), FadeIn(dot1), FadeIn(dot2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(colors[4]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Architectural Workflow: Encoder & Decoder", [
            "The architecture has two main parts.",
            "Encoders digest and encode the input.",
            "Decoders generate the output step-by-step."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Visualizing two main parts
        part1 = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        label1 = Text("Encoder", font_size=24).next_to(part1, UP)
        part2 = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        label2 = Text("Decoder", font_size=24).next_to(part2, UP)
        
        architecture = VGroup(part1, label1, part2, label2)
        self.place_at_grid(part1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'A2')
        self.place_at_grid(part2, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(label2, 'D2')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(architecture))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Representing Encoder digesting input
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['B3'], end=self.grid['B5'], color=WHITE)
        input_data = Text("Input", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(input_data, 'B6')
        
        self.play(Create(arrow), FadeIn(input_data))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Representing Decoder generating output
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=self.grid['E3'], end=self.grid['E5'], color=WHITE)
        output_data = Text("Output", font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(output_data, 'E6')
        
        self.play(Create(arrow2), FadeIn(output_data))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scaling parameters increases model performance.",
            "Larger datasets improve reasoning capabilities.",
            "This leads to complex logic handling."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Scaling Up: Why 'Large' Matters", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        param_dot = Dot(color=BLUE)
        data_cube = Cube(side_length=1.0, fill_opacity=0.5, color=GREEN)
        logic_network = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1, color=YELLOW) for _ in range(5)])
        logic_network.arrange(RIGHT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(param_dot, 'B2', scale_factor=2.0)
        self.play(Create(param_dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(data_cube, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(data_cube))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(logic_network, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(logic_network))

outline.topic: Large Language Models and the Transformer Architecture
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming knowledge

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Next-Word' Prediction Game
sections.content: Define LLMs as sophisticated statistical engines. Introduce the core objective: predicting the next token in a sequence given a context.
sections.example: An octopus is trying to finish the sentence: 'The cat sat on the ___.' Based on statistics, the octopus predicts 'mat' with 85% confidence.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Embeddings – Translating Words to Coordinates
sections.content: Explain that computers don't understand text, only numbers. Introduce high-dimensional vector spaces where similar concepts (e.g., 'King' and 'Queen') are placed close together.
sections.example: Visualizing a 2D map: Placing 'Dog' and 'Puppy' near each other, while 'Spaceship' is on the far end of the map.

sections.title: The Transformer Core: The Self-Attention Mechanism
sections.content: Explain how Transformers process data. Instead of reading word-by-word, 'Attention' allows the model to look at all words in a sentence simultaneously to understand context.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' the model draws a visual 'glowing line' connecting 'it' to 'animal,' ignoring 'street'.

sections.title: Architectural Workflow: Encoder & Decoder
sections.content: Break down the Transformer into two parts: the Encoder (digesting the input) and the Decoder (generating the output step-by-step). Use graphical flow-charts to show information movement.
sections.example: Think of a translator: The Encoder 'reads' the English book and builds a conceptual map; the Decoder 'writes' the French version based on that map.

sections.title: Scaling Up: Why 'Large' Matters
sections.content: Summarize how increasing parameters (weights) and data volume allows models to capture complex logic, nuance, and creativity.
sections.example: A robot learning to walk: A small model trips after one step, while a 'Large' model (trained on billions of movements) performs an elegant, complex dance sequence.
